themes.label: Highly professional, original work written by hand is frequently falsely

entries.text: Highly professional, original work written by hand is frequently falsely flagged as AI-generated, which is incredibly frustrating and unfairly forces researchers to run their own text through humanizing tools [1].

themes.label: Advanced AI detectors like Winston AI are now highly effective

entries.text: Advanced AI detectors like Winston AI are now highly effective at detecting automated "humanizers" and bypassers, defeating their main purpose [2].

themes.label: Automated tools like JenniAI can provide highly irrelevant synonym suggestions,

entries.text: Automated tools like JenniAI can provide highly irrelevant synonym suggestions, repetitive phrasing, and sometimes entirely fail to read or use uploaded PDF documents in the user's library [3].

themes.label: Explaining synonyms, collocations, and contextual examples within actual essays is

entries.text: Explaining synonyms, collocations, and contextual examples within actual essays is vastly superior to rote list cramming [4].

themes.label: Learning vocabulary by topic and in whole phrases (collocations) is

entries.text: Learning vocabulary by topic and in whole phrases (collocations) is far more effective for tests like IELTS than studying isolated individual words [5].

themes.label: Passively reading or being advised against taking notes is highly

entries.text: Passively reading or being advised against taking notes is highly counterproductive; active note-taking and writing down words is crucial for long-term retention [6].

themes.label: Active learning habits—such as underlining unknown words, listing their definitions,

entries.text: Active learning habits—such as underlining unknown words, listing their definitions, and rereading the original context later—drastically help expand vocabulary [7].

themes.label: Utilizing monolingual (English-only) dictionaries, physically carrying pocket card decks,

entries.text: Utilizing monolingual (English-only) dictionaries, physically carrying pocket card decks, and grouping words by roots/synonyms/themes are highly successful strategies [8].

themes.label: Universities should replace lengthy essays with short answer questions or

entries.text: Universities should replace lengthy essays with short answer questions or quizzes to test real comprehension and mitigate widespread AI-facilitated cheating [9].

themes.label: Onscreen vocabulary lessons are much easier to follow if all

entries.text: Onscreen vocabulary lessons are much easier to follow if all target words are listed together at the beginning of the video before the lesson starts [10].

themes.label: Visual learning of vocabulary can be significantly improved by underlining

entries.text: Visual learning of vocabulary can be significantly improved by underlining or highlighting target terms with distinct colors [11].

themes.label: Writers require multiple alternative synonyms (at least 3) for key

entries.text: Writers require multiple alternative synonyms (at least 3) for key terms to prevent repetitive word choices in formal tasks [12].

themes.label: Synonyms are rarely direct, 1-to-1 replacements; users need clear guidance

entries.text: Synonyms are rarely direct, 1-to-1 replacements; users need clear guidance on context, intensity, and register (e.g., the vast difference between "very skinny" and "skeletal") [13].

themes.label: Students need reliable book recommendations or lookup tools to quickly

entries.text: Students need reliable book recommendations or lookup tools to quickly find accurate synonyms when recording newly learned vocabulary [14].

themes.label: Breaking down vocabulary study into small daily goals (e.g., 5

entries.text: Breaking down vocabulary study into small daily goals (e.g., 5 words) paired with daily quizzes builds a robust, long-term memory [15].
